findings.F1: In a falling market (60-day return below −10 %) on the 5-day grid of folds B and C, the tested situation stands out clearly: a negative 10-day return with shrinking 30-day volume is followed by an unusual 5-day move of −3.71 % (t −4.25, 147 cases), and the most-shrunk volume quintile by −3.59 % (t −2.76, 81 cases), while the growing-volume quintiles are +1.81 % (t 1.73) and +0.49 % (t 0.32); this is the idea itself, not a new pattern.
findings.F2: The continuation is stronger in calm falling markets than in agitated ones: with shrinking volume and a negative 10-day return, calm gives −4.07 % over 5 days (t −2.03 with cases of one day together, 79 cases, 34 days) against −3.28 % for agitated (t −1.39, 68 cases); by the coin's own 30-day swing, the falling market's calmest tercile drifts −2.45 % over 5 days (t −2.62, 101 cases), the middle −1.02 % (t −1.10) and the most agitated +0.95 % (t 1.02).
findings.F3: Day by day, a calm falling market also continues down after middling closes: the next day's unusual return is −0.83 % after a close at 20–40 % of the day's range (t −2.07, 199 cases, 120 days) and −1.05 % after 40–60 % (t −2.51, 162 cases); over 2 days, closes above 40 % of the range are followed by −1.13 % (t −1.97, 232 cases). An agitated falling market instead rebounds after a low close, +1.99 % (t 2.62, 146 cases) and grows with range/swing to +3.46 % (t 2.29), and after a fall of more than one daily swing, +2.03 % (t 2.22). That rebound is already held by 039-02, 044-01, 045-01 and 047-01.
findings.F4: In a choppy market (60-day return between −10 % and +10 %), the quintile with the largest 5-day fall is followed by a further unusual 5-day move of −10.54 % (t −4.11, 26 cases), while the other four quintiles lie between −0.26 % and +1.86 % (|t| ≤ 1.11). Next day, a choppy calm close in the lowest tenth of the range is followed by −2.87 % (t −3.06, 19 cases, 16 days). The choppy short cells are empty or thin on the map (choppy agitated short: 0; choppy calm short: 1), but the cases are few.
findings.F5: The book's gain is concentrated in a few windows: the daily returns sum to +0.226 in w7 and +0.10 to +0.13 in each of w13, w14 and w15, against −0.066 in w16 and −0.061 in w17. Per trade, the median is −0.24 % for BTC and −0.32 % for ETH, and XRP's worst trade is −68 %. This fits the failed Calmar of 0.24 more than a missing effect, since the per-case total move is 3.8 times the 0.19 % cost.

ideas.idea: In a falling, calm market, while the coin's 10-day return is still negative, the more its trading volume over the past 30 days has shrunk against the 30 days before, the larger its fall over the next 5 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader keeps the volume dry-up short to falling markets that are still calm, where thin selling drifts on, and stays out of it once the fall turns agitated and starts to rebound.
ideas.name: calm fall volume dry-up

ideas.idea: In a choppy market, the larger the coin's fall over the past 5 days, the further it falls over the next 5 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader in a sideways market treats a sharp 5-day drop as the start of a further decline to short, not as a dip to buy.
ideas.name: choppy sharp fall continues
